meta.note: English source of the terms and privacy page (/{lang}/terms). It is published only when src/modules/subscriptions/domain/terms.ts accepts it: a named owner, a last-updated date, an English review by that owner, a privacy contact, a consent version and a counsel review of exactly this English and version, or, for the pilot only, the owner's recorded waiver of it (counselWaiver, held to the same rules). Values starting with PLACEHOLDER are refused. Any change to the text, the contact or the version needs a new counsel review (python3 scripts/review_translations.py --content --mark-counsel-reviewed --reviewer NAME --reviewed-on DATE) or a new decision by the owner (--waive-counsel --reviewer OWNER --reviewed-on DATE --reason TEXT). Translations: data/catalogue/translations/content/<lang>.json, keys terms.*.

sections.heading: What we keep
lines: If you sign up for text alerts, we keep four things.
Your phone number.
Your language.
Your neighbourhood: Thorncliffe Park or Flemingdon Park.
Choices you make if you want to, such as your building, your floor and the groups you belong to.
If an ambassador could not reach you or found you needed help, the Hub keeps your number and floor to follow up. It keeps them for up to 24 hours after the alert ends.
We do not ask for your name. We do not ask for your unit number, your email or a password. We do not keep them.
If you do not sign up, we keep nothing about you. This app sets no cookies. It does not keep the questions you type.

sections.heading: Who handles your information
lines: Four companies help us run the service. They handle information for us.
Twilio sends the text messages. It handles your phone number and our messages to you. It may do this outside Canada.
Cohere translates alerts and helps match questions you type in search. It never gets your phone number. It may work outside Canada.
Vercel runs the website. Its servers are in Montreal. If there is an outage, it may use servers in the United States.
Supabase keeps the database that holds your number, language, neighbourhood and choices. The database is in Canada.
Twilio keeps a copy of each text, with your phone number. This includes your replies. The Hub deletes these copies from Twilio after the pilot ends.
We never sell your phone number, and we never share it or your agreement to get texts with anyone for marketing. The four companies above use it only to run this service.

sections.heading: Who owns the data
lines: The community owns the data. The Hub looks after it for you and your neighbours.

sections.heading: How to stop
lines: Reply STOP to any text from the Hub. Or reply 0, then reply 0 again to confirm.
When you stop, we delete your subscription. That means we delete your phone number and your choices. We cannot get them back.
After that, we send you nothing.
Twilio's copies of the texts we sent you and of your replies stay until the Hub deletes them from Twilio after the pilot ends.

sections.heading: Who can sign up
lines: You must be 16 or older to sign up.
If you are younger than 16, a parent or guardian must help you sign up.

sections.heading: About the messages
lines: Hub staff check every alert before it is sent.
Because of this, a message may not be sent overnight.
How often we text depends on what happens in your building. Message and data rates may apply. Reply HELP for help.

sections.heading: Questions and your information
lines: To see what we hold about you, or to fix it, contact our privacy contact.
Hub staff will call your number back to check that it is yours. Then they will tell you what we hold. If something is wrong, they will fix it.
